transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-29 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (CS), Sam (CTO, Irislytics), Maya (ML Eng), Leo (PM), Anita (Infra)

Optional auto-summary: (auto) KV cache is showing promising cost reductions on medium-length prompts; batching still useful but needs policy tuning to meet Irislytics' 200ms tail latency SLO for short queries.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:06] Sam: sam here.
[00:07] Maya: maya on.
[00:08] Leo: leo.
[00:09] Anita: anita here.
[00:12] Priya: priya, redwood se.
[00:15] Jordan: cool, we ran the set of bench runs I promised last week, priya ran an extended kv-cache pass, we'll share the sheet in a sec. high level, we saw around ~30% tokens-per-dollar improvement on your medium prompt mix with prefix caching. priya, wanna summarize numbers?
[00:35] Priya: yeah, sure. so we used the Irislytics prompt set of 6000 samples, sequence lengths average ~420 tokens, variance high. baseline was hosted small model variant (redwood-gpt-medium-q8) no cache. with KV prefix caching enabled we saw median cost drop 32% and mean tokens/sec per dollar up from 12.4k to 16.2k, so roughly +30% throughput per dollar. caveat: when we increased batching aggressively (batch size 32) we got higher tokens/sec but saw p95 latency go up 12-18% for short queries.
[01:12] Maya: sorry quick q, when you say p95 latency up, what's the absolute? like are we hitting our 200ms tail SLO?
[01:18] Priya: good question. short queries (<= 64 tokens) baseline p95 was ~170ms on dedicated medium GPU; with batch 32 it rose to ~205-220ms. with moderate batching (8-12) and kv-cache we generally stayed around 180-190ms.
[01:35] Leo: so there's a sweet spot tradeoff. tokens/sec/$ improves more with bigger batches but latency penalty kills some UX flows. is that accurate?
[01:42] Jordan: yeah exactly, it's classic. for your interactive product flows I'd recommend either small batching plus KV-caching, or use dynamic batching policy for background scoring.
[01:50] Sam: got it. can you explain the KV cache hit rate? what percent of prefixes matched?
[01:56] Priya: hit rate was about 46% across that sample set. it varies heavily by user session patterns; for long-form followups the hit rate climbs to 70%. note also cache TTL matters — we used a 24-hour TTL for these runs.
[02:15] Maya: did you check any hallucination/quality diffs when using cached kv? sometimes reusing KV can bias later tokens.
[02:22] Priya: we ran a quality check on 800 samples. overall token-level perplexity differences were negligible, and human review flagged ~2% quality regressions, mostly around entity substitution in extremely context-specific prompts. we logged those examples in the sheet.
[02:39] Anita: security question — where is that cache stored in hosted mode? we need to know for compliance.
[02:44] Jordan: good call. for hosted we persist kv in our managed cache partitioning with encryption at rest; if you do Private (VPC) deployment you can host KV storage in your subnet and use your KMS. i'll attach the security doc.
[02:58] Sam: perfect. also timeline: we said pilot decision by end of Q1. is that still reasonable?
[03:03] Jordan: yep, seems aligned.
[03:06] Priya: quick demo: i'm going to talk through a couple runs — forgive the audio, screen share in the sheet.
[03:12] Speaker 2: (unintelligible)
[03:15] Priya: ok, on slide one — the baseline run, cost per 1M tokens was $X (redacted in sheet), with kv we estimate $Y, net ~32% lower. also note we tested model quantization q4 vs q8, q4 bought more cost savings but had ~4% quality delta on your eval set.
[03:40] Maya: can you repeat the q4 vs q8 numbers? we haven't validated q4 quality on our prompts yet.
[03:45] Priya: sure — q8 baseline, q4 gave about +18% tokens/sec/$ but we saw ~3-5% higher error rate on entity recall tests. depends on your risk tolerance.
[03:55] Jordan: also want to call out multi-tenant noise — on shared hosted we saw variance on p95 depending on cluster noise; Dedicated gives more predictable p95.
[04:06] Sam: for enterprise we prefer predictability. what's Redwood Dedicated pricing delta for the pool size we discussed?
[04:12] Jordan: i'll attach updated pricing. ballpark, Dedicated reserved pool for your throughput needs is ~1.6-1.8x hosted for pure compute but with better latency SLOs and no multi-tenant interference. net unit economics often ends up better at scale because you can push batching and caching more aggressively.
[04:30] Leo: what about private deployment — we'd likely need VPC + our own KMS. any blockers?
[04:35] Priya: we support VPC private control plane and optional on-prem KV. the main blocker is network egress for telemetry — if you want zero egress we can do air-gapped with a slightly different ops bill. Anita: (murmur) we need that note.
[04:50] Anita: yeah air-gapped is a heavier lift. our preference is VPC with customer-managed KMS.
[04:55] Priya: that's supported. we'll need your KMS ARN and some firewall rules. i'll send a list.
[05:00] Jordan: back to economics — tokens/sec/$ is useful, but for product decisions you should look at tokens-per-concurrent-dollar and also per-request cost for short interactive queries. Priya, we had that chart?
[05:10] Priya: yes, chart 3 in the sheet shows tokens-per-concurrent-dollar across batch sizes: batch 1 gives 9.8k tokens/sec/$, batch 8 gives 14.5k, batch 32 gives 21.4k but p95 latency rises. so if your feature is 1-3s response it's fine, but for 200ms edge cases you want smaller batches.
[05:33] Maya: can we do hybrid? small batch/kv for interactive flows, big batch for async scoring?
[05:36] Jordan: exactly that's the recommended pattern. route by endpoint: /chat-interactive uses batch<=8 + kv, /batch-scoring uses batch>=16 + aggressive cache + quantized models.
[05:45] Sam: are there any throughput limits that would block our planned 100 qps baseline?
[05:50] Priya: not on Dedicated sized to your commit. On hosted, we can autoscale but you may see cold-start variability; for 100 qps steady, Dedicated is more predictable.
[05:59] Leo: earlier you mentioned cache TTL. can we do per-tenant TTLs or finer control? some customers need 1-hour TTLs.
[06:06] Priya: yes per-tenant TTLs supported on Private and Dedicated. hosted supports TTLs but with shared policy limits; we can raise limits for enterprise pilots.
[06:14] Anita: encryption at rest — we need to confirm HSM/KMS options and audit logs retention.
[06:19] Jordan: yes SOC2 plus audit logs available at the enterprise level, and you can bring-your-own-KMS for private/dedicated; i'll include the SOC2 artifact and KMS integration guide.
[06:28] Sam: quick pricing question: if we hit a 30% unit cost reduction from KV, does Redwood share any uplift guarantee on committed capacity?
[06:34] Jordan: we don't guarantee savings, but we can model committed reserved pricing that makes Dedicated attractive. we do invoice credits for missed SLOs per contract.
[06:41] Maya: about the 2% quality regressions you mentioned earlier — can you surface examples inline? we'd like to triage which are unacceptable.
[06:47] Priya: yes, the sheet has links to the sample cases. most are edge-case entity mismatches in very specific prompts; i'd flag that as low-risk, but of course you should vet.
[06:58] Sam: for the next run can you include a per-endpoint estimated $/1000 requests for our interactive prompt mix? that'll make procurement easier.
[07:05] Jordan: yup we can compute $/1k requests for the exact mix (we'll use median length and use weighted mix). adding to next steps.
[07:10] Evan (CS): also can we get a short README for the bench harness so Maya's team can reproduce?
[07:14] Priya: yes will push the harness and TF/Py client snippet. note: some flags are internal (like kernel tuning) but we'll expose the knobs you need.
[07:23] Sam: any competitors on this convo? we demoed at Anthropic last month and they pitched a latency-optimized path; curious if you have similar recommendations.
[07:31] Jordan: Anthropic focuses on model-side optimizations; our differentiation is unified runtime + routing + caching controls. for latency, we optimize kernel selection and KV policy.
[07:40] Maya: there's mention of quantization q4 earlier — for safety we might hold off on q4 for customer-facing flows until we validate.
[07:46] Priya: sensible. q4 for background scoring only.
[07:50] Leo: timeline check: we want final pilot numbers for procurement by mid-December. is that doable?
[07:56] Jordan: yes, with the bench results and pricing we'll hit that.
[08:00] Priya: i'll schedule the 10k-token benchmark run tonight and aim to share updated sheet by Dec 3.
[08:05] Maya: thanks. one more curious thing — you mentioned KV cache storage in private deploys. what's the expected ops overhead on our side?
[08:12] Priya: for Private with your KV service, the overhead is mostly provisioning storage + setting up TTL policies; we provide helm charts and an operator for lifecycle. expected 1-2 engineer days to stand up in dev.
[08:24] Anita: ok that's fine.
[08:26] Jordan: quick recap before we close?
[08:29] Sam: sure. please repeat the 3 bullets we'll get.
[08:32] Jordan: 1) Priya runs extended KV+batch bench and shares tokens/sec/$ and per-endpoint $/1k by 2026-12-03. 2) Jordan shares updated pilot pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison by 2026-12-01. 3) Maya validates sample outputs and reports regressions by 2026-12-06; Anita provides VPC/KMS constraints doc by 2026-12-02.
[08:53] Leo: i'll take scheduling for the infra follow-up during week of Dec 7.
[08:56] Priya: couple of quick clarifying notes — when we send the harness it's got a "kv_on" flag, a "batch_size" param and a "quant_mode" param. tune batch_size per endpoint.
[09:07] Maya: noted.
[09:10] Jordan: any last questions?
[09:12] Sam: none from me, thanks all.
[09:14] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll send notes. end call.

Post-call notes (auto): attached sheet: irislytics-kv-batch-results-20261129.xlsx (link). Key signals: ~32% cost reduction with KV cache; q4 quantization adds ~18% tokens/sec/$ but small quality tradeoffs; batching increases tokens/sec/$ substantially but linearly increases p95 for short queries; Dedicated recommended for 100 qps baseline for predictability.

References shared: pricing-sheet-v3.pdf (link), SOC2-and-KMS-integration.md (link), bench-harness-repo (link).

Caveats in transcript: occasional misattribs and filler words; see action items for owners and due dates.
